title: Naming: DecodedBlock (uuencoding) vs DecodedPart (yencoding) for same concept
description:
## Finding

uuencoding::DecodedBlock and yencoding::DecodedPart are analogous types — both are the result returned by the crate's decode() function representing a single successfully decoded binary payload with metadata. They differ only in name.

## Locations

- uuencoding/src/lib.rs: pub struct DecodedBlock { pub data: Vec<u8>, pub metadata: BlockMetadata, pub is_truncated: bool, pub was_limit_hit: bool }
- yencoding/src/lib.rs: pub struct DecodedPart { pub data: Vec<u8>, pub metadata: YencMetadata, pub part: Option<u32>, ... }

## Impact

A caller using both crates (e.g. mime-tree, which depends on both) must remember two unrelated type names for the same concept. A maintainer adding a third encoding crate has no consistent naming convention to follow. The divergence becomes load-bearing when uuencoding-multi and yencoding-multi embed these types: uuencoding-multi's ReassembledFile was shaped to match DecodedBlock, but yencoding-multi's Assembler::add_part takes &yencoding::DecodedPart — the asymmetry propagates upward.
close_reason: DecodedBlock vs DecodedPart — different names reflect the different encoding formats (UU blocks vs yEnc parts). Renaming would be breaking.
